title_ar: ردود على الأسئلة الواردة إلى الموقع ج 1
title_en: Responses to the Questions Received by the Site, Part 1
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه إلى يوم الدين، بعض الإجابات على بعض الأسئلة الواردة على الموقع • الدفعة الأولى من الأسئلة: عنوان الفتوى: ارتضاع الرجل لبن زوجته السؤال الأول: هل يجوز للرجل أن يرتضع لبن زوجته؟ الجواب: لا ليس للرجل ارتضاع لبن زوجته ، لأن ذلك ليس من الاستمتاع وإنما يجوز له المتعة؛ أي الاستمتاع بما أحله الله منها، والإرضاع ليس من تلك المتعة، لكن مذهب الجمهور أنه لو ارتضع لبنها فإنه لا يحرمها ذلك عليه ولا يخرجها عن عصمته خلافا لأم المومنين عائشة رضي الله عنها ولبعض علماء السلف فإنهم يرون أن الكبير تنتشر محرميته بالرضاع واستدلوا بحديث سلمة بنت سهيل أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمرها أن ترضع سالما مولى أبي حذيفة وهو كبير، ومذهب الجمهور قصر انتشار الحرمة بالرضاع على الحولين، لقول الله تعالى " والوالدات يرضعن أولادهن حولين كاملين"، ولقوله تعالى "وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا، ولقوله تعالى " وفصاله في عامين". وحديث سهلة يجاب عنه بأنه حالة خاصة لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما أذن لها في إرضاع من كانت قد تبنته في الجاهلية ولا تبني بعد ذلكفإن التبني أبطله الإسلام بعد نزول آية سورة الأحزاب فلم يعد الإنسان ممكنا من تبني الغير بل يجب نسبته إلى أبيه كما قال الله تعالى " أدعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله". وهذه المرأة كانت تبنت سالما مدة طويلة فأصبحت بمثابة أمه فلذلك أذن لها في إرضاعه واليوم لا توجد امرأة قد تبنت رجلا على وجه شرعي فالتبني ليس جائزا. عنوان الفتوى:الاقتراض من البنك الربوي لأجل الزواج السؤال الثاني: أنا شاب مقدم على الزواج فهل يجوز لي أن أقترض من البنك وأنا موظف للدولة في مجال التعليم ؟ الجواب أن القرض الربوي لا يحل للإنسان إلا إذا اضطر له فإن الله تعالى يقول: " يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقو الله وذرو ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين، ويقول تعالى " يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا الربا أضعافا مضاعفة واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين"، فلا يحل للإنسان الإقدام على أخذ القرض الربوي إلا مضطرا والضرورة مثل أن يخاف على نفسه الزنا وأن لا يجد ما يدفعه مهرا ، وهنا نصيحة للشباب أن كثيرا من الناس يظن أن الزواج له تكاليف كبيرة وأنه لا يمكن أن يقدم عليه إلا إذا جمع أموالا طائلة فخير الأنكحة أقلها تكاليفا وخير النساء أقلهن مهرا ، وقد ثبت في حديث ابن عباس " أن أفضل هذه الأمة أقلها صداقا، وثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال عليكم خير النساء صلح نساء قريش؛ أحناه على ولد في صغره، وأرعاه على زوج في ذات يده وأرضاه بالقليل، فإذا اضطر الإنسان ولم يجد ما يكون صداقا مع أنه لم يكن يأتي بسرف ولا بخيلة ولم يجد من يقرضه ولا من يتاجر معه بدين، فحينئذ تكون حالته يمكن أن تنزل منزل الضرورة وتحتاج إلى استفتاء خاص ممن يطلع على ظروفه وشؤونه وهل هو صاحب رخصة أم لا . عنوان الفتوى:صيام يوم عرفة باختلاف المطالع السؤال الثالث: أنا طالب في ماليزيا ويوم عرفة عندنا يوافق يوم السادس عشر من نوفمبر بينما الحجاج سوف يقفون بعرفة يوم الخامس عشر من نوفمبر، كيف أصوم يوم عرفة ؟ أي اليوم الذي يقف فيه الحجاج وهو يوافق في ماليزيا العيد ؟ الجواب أنه يصوم اليوم التاسع من ذي الحجة على مقتضى الوطن الذي هو فيه والبلد الذي هو فيه وذلك أن أهل كل بلد عندما تختلف المطالع ويختلف التوقيت، لهم وقتهم كما أنه لا يجوز له أن يصلي بصلاة أهل مكة فكذلك لا يصوم بصيامهم، فاليوم عند أهل مكة يبدأ بوسط النهار أو آخره عند أهل ماليزيا لذلك فيوم عرفة في حقه هو ليس هو اليوم الذي يقف فيه الحجاج بل هو اليوم التاسع من ذي الحجة. ------------ عنوان الفتوى: حكم ما يسمى ب " لحْجَابْ" واستعمال الجداول والأوفاق بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم بعد التحية والسلام، أطلب منكم صالح الدعاء.. نسأل الله أن يحقق رجاءه وأن يستجيب دعاءه. أطلب منكم توضيح الحكم الشرعي لما يسمى عندنا ب "لحْجَابْ"، وهل يجوز استعمال الاوفاق أو ما يسمى بالجداول ؟؟. الجواب أن لحجاب يطلق على بعض الرقى والتمائم ونحوها وهو اسم عام يشمل الصحيح والفاسد ففيه ما هو صحيح مثل الرقيا بالقرآن والحديث الصحيح، وفيه ما هو باطل مثل ما كان من السحر ومن علوم الشر علم الجدول فعلم الجداول والأوفاق كله من علوم الشر فلا يحل للمسلم الاشتغال به ولا تعليقه، واختلف أهل العلم فيما يحل السحر منه فقد ذهب بعضهم إلى جوازه لأنه نافع غير ضار ولأن الله تعالى يقول " فيتعلمون ما يضرهم ولا ينفعهم " فهذه خاصية السحر فهو يضر ولا ينفع، أما ما ينفع ولا يضر فهو ليس داخلا في تعريفه ولكن مذهب الجمهور أن ذلك لا يحل مطلقا وأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبطله بقوله: " من أحدث في أمرنا هذا ما ليس منه فهو رد"، وفي رواية لمسلم من عمل عملا ليس عليه أمرنا فهو رد". فهذا ليس مما جاء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من عند لله فلذلك لا يشتغل به المسلم ولا يحل له الإقدام عليه. عنوان الفتوى: القسم على الأرواح وخطابها سؤال ... موضوع عمت به البلوى وهو القسم على الروحاني هل يجوز، وهل هناك روحانيون مكلفون بخدمات لحجاب؟؟ الجواب أن الروحانية المقصود به الأرواح عموما ولا يحل القسم عليها ولا خطابها لكنها موجودة فالأرواح لا تعدم ومنها أرواح شريرة وارواح طيبة فالأرواح الطيبة أرواح أهل الإيمان والتقوى والأرواح الشريرة أرواح أهل الحسد والخبث والكفر والنفاق، وهي تشمل الإنس والجن فكل له أرواح، لكن لا يقسم عليها ولا تخاطب. انتهى.
body_en:
In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and may God bless our Prophet Muhammad and his family and his Companions and all who take guidance from his guidance until the Day of Judgement. Some answers to some of the questions received by the site.

• The first batch of questions:

## Title of the fatwa: A man's suckling his wife's milk

**Question one: Is it permissible for a man to suckle his wife's milk?**

The answer: No, it is not for a man to suckle his wife's milk, because that is not a form of enjoyment. What is permissible to him is enjoyment — that is, taking pleasure in what God has made lawful to him of her — and suckling is not part of that enjoyment. But the position of the majority is that if he did suckle her milk, that does not make her forbidden to him, nor does it take her out of his marriage bond; contrary to the Mother of the Believers Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and to some of the scholars of the early generations, for they hold that an adult's marriage impediment does spread through suckling. They adduced as evidence the report of Salamah bint Suhayl, that the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — commanded her to suckle Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfah, he being an adult. The position of the majority is to restrict the spread of the impediment through suckling to the two years, by the words of God Most High {And mothers suckle their children two full years} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:233), and by His words, exalted is He, {And his bearing and his weaning are thirty months} (Sūrat al-Aḥqāf 46:15), and by His words, exalted is He, {and his weaning is within two years} (Sūrat Luqmān 31:14).

The report of Sahlah is answered by saying that it was a special case, because the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — permitted her only to suckle one whom she had adopted in the age of ignorance; and there is no adoption after that, for Islam abolished adoption after the revelation of the verse of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb. So a person is no longer able to adopt another; rather he must be ascribed to his own father, as God Most High said: {Call them by their fathers' names; that is more equitable in God's sight} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:5). This woman had adopted Salim over a long period, so that she had become in the position of his mother, and for that reason he permitted her to suckle him. Today there is no woman who has adopted a man in a lawful manner, for adoption is not permissible.

## Title of the fatwa: Borrowing from an interest-based bank for the sake of marriage

**Question two: I am a young man about to marry. Is it permissible for me to borrow from the bank, being a state employee in the field of education?**

The answer is that a usurious loan is not lawful for a person unless he is driven to it by necessity; for God Most High says: {O you who believe, be mindful of God and give up what remains of usurious gain (ribā), if you are believers} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:278). And He says, exalted is He: {O you who believe, do not consume usurious gain, doubled and multiplied; and be mindful of God, that you may prosper. And guard yourselves against the Fire that has been prepared for the unbelievers} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:130–131). So it is not lawful for a person to proceed to take a usurious loan except under compulsion of necessity; and necessity (ḍarūrah) is, for example, that he fears fornication for himself and finds nothing to pay as the bridal gift (mahr).

Here is a word of advice for young men. Many people think that marriage carries great costs, and that one cannot embark upon it unless he has amassed vast sums; but the best of marriages is the least costly, and the best of women are those whose bridal gift is least. It is established in the report of Ibn Abbas that "the best of this community are those whose bridal payment is least"; and it is established from the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: take to yourselves the best of women, the righteous women of Quraysh: the most tender of them towards a child in his infancy, the most careful of them over a husband in respect of what his hand possesses, and the most content with little. So if a person is driven by necessity and finds nothing to serve as a bridal payment — he not having been extravagant nor making a display — and finds no one to lend to him and no one to trade with him on credit, then at that point his case can be placed in the position of necessity; and it requires a particular ruling from someone acquainted with his circumstances and his affairs, and with whether he is entitled to the dispensation (rukhṣah) or not.

## Title of the fatwa: Fasting the day of Arafah where the moon-sighting horizons differ

**Question three: I am a student in Malaysia, and the day of Arafah with us falls on the sixteenth of November, while the pilgrims will stand at Arafah on the fifteenth of November. How am I to fast the day of Arafah — that is, the day on which the pilgrims stand, which in Malaysia coincides with the Eid?**

The answer is that he fasts the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah as determined by the country he is in and the land he is in. That is because the people of each land, where the moon-sighting horizons differ and the timing differs, have their own time. Just as it is not permissible for him to pray by the prayer of the people of Mecca, so too he does not fast by their fast; for the day among the people of Mecca begins at the middle of the day, or at its end, for the people of Malaysia. Therefore the day of Arafah, with respect to him, is not the day on which the pilgrims stand, but the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah.

------------

## Title of the fatwa: The ruling on what is called "lḥjāb", and the use of the tables and the magic squares

**In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. After greetings and peace, I ask of you your good supplication.. [We ask God to fulfil his hope and to answer his supplication.] I ask you to clarify the legal ruling on what is called among us "lḥjāb", and whether it is permissible to use the awfāq, or what are called the jadāwil??**

The answer is that "lḥjāb" is applied to certain healing recitations, amulets and the like. It is a general name taking in both the sound and the defective: within it is what is sound, such as healing recitation with the Qur'an and with sound hadith; and within it is what is void, such as what belongs to sorcery. Among the sciences of evil is the science of the table; for the science of the tables (jadāwil) and of the magic squares (awfāq) is entirely among the sciences of evil, so it is not lawful for a Muslim to occupy himself with it, nor to hang it upon himself.

The people of knowledge differed over that which undoes sorcery. Some of them held it permissible, because it is beneficial and not harmful, and because God Most High says {and they learn what harms them and does not benefit them} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:102) — this being the distinguishing property of sorcery, that it harms and does not benefit; whereas what benefits and does not harm does not fall within its definition. But the position of the majority is that it is not lawful at all, and that the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — nullified it by his words: «Whoever introduces into this affair of ours what is not of it, it is rejected»; and in a transmission of Muslim: «Whoever performs an act which our affair is not upon, it is rejected.» This is not among what the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — brought from God, so a Muslim does not occupy himself with it, and it is not lawful for him to embark upon it.

## Title of the fatwa: Swearing upon the spirits and addressing them

**Question ... a matter with which affliction has become general, namely swearing upon the spirit-being: is it permissible? And are there spirit-beings charged with services of the lḥjāb??**

The answer is that by "the spirit-beings" spirits in general are meant. It is not lawful to swear upon them nor to address them. But they do exist — spirits are not non-existent — and among them are evil spirits and good spirits: the good spirits are the spirits of the people of faith and God-consciousness, and the evil spirits are the spirits of the people of envy, malice, unbelief and hypocrisy. They take in both humans and jinn, for each has its spirits. But one does not swear upon them, and they are not addressed. End.

flags.arabic: لحْجَابْ ... الجداول ... الأوفاق ... فيما يحل السحر منه
flags.context: the fourth fatwa, on amulets and the science of the tables
options: leave 'lḥjāb' transliterated with the Sheikh's own definition beside it; render jadāwil as 'the tables' and awfāq as 'the magic squares'
render 'lḥjāb' as 'the amulet'
render jadāwil and awfāq together as 'talismanic squares'
flags.note: IMPORTANT for the glossary. This single answer contains two of the terms listed at style guide section 13 as glossary additions still pending, and supplies the Sheikh's own working definitions of them. 'لحْجَابْ' is Hassaniyya — the questioner marks it as local ('what is called among us') and it is vocalised in dialect orthography with the Mauritanian definite article; it is left transliterated, because the Sheikh's whole point is that it is a general name covering both lawful and unlawful practices, and any single English word would decide the question he is answering. 'الجداول' (al-jadāwil) and 'الأوفاق' (awfāq) are the lettered tables and numerical squares of the talismanic sciences. 'فيما يحل السحر منه' is al-nushrah, the third of the pending terms, here described but not named. All three should be settled from this record, since it is the clearest definition of them in the slice.

flags.arabic: يشمل الصحيح والفاسد ففيه ما هو صحيح ... وفيه ما هو باطل
flags.context: the classification of practices covered by the name lḥjāb
options: sound / defective / void, by the fixed glossary renderings
valid / invalid
permitted / forbidden
flags.note: Three glossary terms fall in two sentences and the fixed renderings are used. Note particularly that ṣaḥīḥ appears twice in this answer in its two different senses — 'the sound' as against the defective, and 'sound hadith' as a grading — and the English distinguishes them as the glossary directs. None of the three may be rendered as 'forbidden': they concern validity, not sin, and the Sheikh gives his prohibition separately, in the words 'it is not lawful'.

flags.arabic: واستدلوا بحديث سلمة بنت سهيل ... وحديث سهلة يجاب عنه
flags.context: the name of the Companion in the first fatwa
options: read as Sahlah bint Suhayl, as the same record gives it two sentences later and as record 670 gives it
leave both forms unresolved
flags.note: The record names her 'سلمة بنت سهيل' and then, two sentences later, 'حديث سهلة'. The two forms cannot both be right and the record itself supplies the correction. Record 670 in this same slice gives her as 'سهلة بنت سهيل بن عمرو'. Both forms are left as served in body_ar and reproduced in the English, so the inconsistency stays visible rather than being silently harmonised.

flags.arabic: أنا طالب في ماليزيا ويوم عرفة عندنا يوافق يوم السادس عشر من نوفمبر
flags.context: the third fatwa, against the record's CMS timestamp of 13 March 2011
options: treat the CMS timestamp as an upload date and note that the question itself dates from around November of an earlier year
treat the CMS timestamp as the date of the answer
flags.note: STRONG corroboration that the CMS timestamps are upload dates. The questioner writes that the pilgrims will stand at Arafah on 15 November and that Arafah falls locally on 16 November — a configuration that places the question in mid-November, whereas the record is stamped 13 March 2011. A question written for a Hajj season cannot have been asked in March. The date must not be presented to readers as the date of the fatwa.

flags.arabic: وتحتاج إلى استفتاء خاص ممن يطلع على ظروفه وشؤونه وهل هو صاحب رخصة أم لا
flags.context: the closing of the second fatwa, on borrowing from a bank
options: render exactly — he declines to rule on this questioner's case and refers him on
report the answer as permitting the loan under necessity
report the answer as forbidding the loan
flags.note: CRITICAL. The Sheikh does NOT answer this questioner's question. He states the general ruling — a usurious loan is not lawful except under necessity — defines what necessity would look like, urges that marriage costs be kept low, and then expressly refers the man to someone acquainted with his circumstances to decide whether the dispensation applies to him. The English preserves that refusal exactly. Reporting this as 'the Sheikh permits borrowing from a bank to marry' would be false; so would reporting it as a flat prohibition. The answer must be displayed whole.

flags.arabic: عليكم خير النساء صلح نساء قريش؛ أحناه على ولد في صغره، وأرعاه على زوج في ذات يده وأرضاه بالقليل
flags.context: the report quoted about the women of Quraysh
options: render the wording exactly as served, reading 'صلح' as 'the righteous of', and add no attribution
align the wording with the well-known transmission
flags.note: The wording as served is damaged and expanded. 'صلح نساء قريش' appears to stand for 'صالح نساء قريش', the righteous women of Quraysh; the well-known transmission opens differently, and the closing phrase 'and the most content with little' is not part of it. The Sheikh gives no collection and no grading, only 'it is established from the Prophet'. Per style guide section 4 nothing has been added and nothing aligned; per section 11 the damaged wording is left visible. Both this and the Ibn Abbas report before it need checking against the printed sources by a reviewer.

flags.arabic: مع أنه لم يكن يأتي بسرف ولا بخيلة
flags.context: the conditions attached to the plea of necessity
options: read 'خيلة' as 'خُيَلاء' — vanity or display
read it as 'حيلة' — a stratagem
leave unresolved
flags.note: 'خيلة' as served is not a standard form. Paired with 'سرف' (extravagance) the sense of vain display fits the argument, which is about a man who has kept his marriage costs modest; 'حيلة', a legal stratagem, would also fit a discussion of necessity but sits less well with 'extravagance'. Rendered at the first reading and flagged.

flags.arabic: بعد التحية والسلام، أطلب منكم صالح الدعاء.. نسأل الله أن يحقق رجاءه وأن يستجيب دعاءه
flags.context: the opening of the fourth question
options: read the second sentence as an editorial or the Sheikh's interjection inside the quoted question, and mark it
read the whole passage as the questioner's own words
flags.note: The questioner asks for the Sheikh's supplication in the first person; the sentence that follows speaks of him in the third person ('his hope', 'his supplication') and so cannot be his. It is an interjection by whoever was transcribing or answering. The English puts it in square brackets to mark the change of voice, which the Arabic marks only by the shift of person.

flags.arabic: ولا تبني بعد ذلكفإن التبني ... من عند لله ... لأم المومنين ... اتقو الله وذرو ما بقي
flags.context: orthographic and spacing defects across the record
options: leave all as served and record them
normalise
flags.note: Five defects, all left as served in body_ar: 'ذلكفإن' with no word space; 'من عند لله' missing the alif of Allah; 'المومنين' without hamza; and 'اتقو' and 'ذرو' without the final silent alif in a Qur'anic quotation. The last of these matters most, since it falls inside quoted scripture; per style guide section 11 it is not restored. The record also leaves one quotation mark unclosed, at 'وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا'.

translator_notes: A compilation of five written fatwas with real answers, headed 'the first batch of questions'. Together with records 670 and 672 it shows that the written fatwa material in this corpus is substantially larger than the inventory's count of two.

Part numbering in this series does not follow the CMS dates: this record is 'Part 1' and is stamped 13 March 2011, while record 672, 'Part 2', carries an earlier stamp. The parts should be ordered by their own numbering, not by the timestamps.

The first fatwa overlaps in subject with two answers in record 670, on the suckling of an adult, and the reasoning differs in emphasis: there the dispensation is explained as particular to Sahlah and Salim alone, here as resting on the prior adoption which Islam then abolished. The two are compatible but not identical, and a reviewer should read them together.

Qur'anic references have been supplied in the English where the source gives none; this is presentation, not restoration, and body_ar is untouched. The renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The row of dashes between the third and fourth fatwas is the source's own separator and is kept.
